title: Names: floor, rock, wall, gate; a planet surface that a breach patches instead of rebuilding
context: Owner, 2026-09-15: agree the names for the planet's open ground, its raised lattice, the man-made wall segments and the gate. Rock that tank shells can break should also break under the orbital laser. Breaking rock causes a jarring ~0.5 s hitch, which shows on a single tank shell and badly when the laser takes several rocks in a row, as if something is redrawn. Try hiding the lines on the rock tops for a more uniform look. The beam also shows a straight dividing line, especially on rock.
outcome: Names, agreed by the owner: FLOOR is open ground (PATH cells); ROCK is the planet's own raised lattice (BLOCKED cells, the planet mesh's rock layer); WALL is the man-made segments either side of the gate (plan.walls, the kit wall); GATE is the armoured opening (plan.gate). The laser lab's labels and LASER_BURN's comments use them; td-tab.js still says 'wall cell' for rock and is not renamed in this change. b563a74 made rock cells burn under the laser as a tank shell breaks them (structure and socket cells anchored), with LASER_BURN.rock 0.5. 357d98b adds createStoryPlanetSurface: fixed per-cell and per-edge slots, so refreshCells() patches a breached cell and its four edges by addUpdateRange and nothing is rebuilt. rockLines is 'all', 'rim' (only where rock meets floor) or 'none', and the lab defaults to rim. The lab's beam, glow and smoke now land on the real ground height (terrace floor, or rock top) instead of 4 m inside a rock.
alternatives: Keep rebuilding the whole planet mesh and throttle it to one rebuild per 0.3 s (the first cut in b563a74); rejected because every rebuild is still a ~150-200 ms hitch, only rarer.

A cell-height data texture sampled in the vertex shader, so a breach writes one texel; not chosen now because the fixed-slot buffers keep the plain MeshBasicMaterial and vertex colours and patch in microseconds, at the cost of drawing collapsed slots.

Port the patch into td-tab.js's buildGeometry for the game's tank shells in the same change; deferred because td-tab.js is outside this change's files and carries the architecture line budget. It is the follow-up that removes the game's hitch.
evidence: Node benchmark on the baked story planet (71,314 cells): buildStoryPlanetMesh 201 ms; createStoryPlanetSurface 46 ms to build; refreshCells on one cell 0.002 ms. Opening a rock cell ringed by rock added exactly 4 rock sides and 4 rim lines, and closing it again restored the side buffer byte for byte.
npm test green (106 test programs passed) and npm run check green on 357d98b.

Not browser-verified: the memory guardrail stayed at WARN. The straight line on the beam is diagnosed from reading (the flat beam ribbon placed at floor height inside a 4 m rock) because the owner's two photos in ~/Downloads could not be opened here.
